key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, travel speed, and welding current shape molten-pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability.
engineering_relevance: These parameter–response relationships can guide welding optimization for low-expansion Invar tooling used in aerospace composite manufacturing.
method: High-speed photography of pool evolution and arc behavior
Comparison across laser power, welding speed, and current ranges
evidence_signal: Across 5–6 kW, higher power increased penetration and keyhole size; across 0.5–0.8 m/min, higher speed reduced penetration and weld width; across 150–170 A, higher current widened the weld and improved arc stability.
watch_item: The abstract reports trends over limited parameter ranges but provides no quantitative prediction errors or weld mechanical-property validation.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
